title: A Transparent Photonic Chip That Can Bend
mediaSource: MIT flexible transparent silicon photonics chip wearable AR display

scenes.title: What if a computer chip could bend and stay transparent?
scenes.narration: MIT researchers have developed a scalable way to make silicon photonic chips flexible and transparent.

scenes.title: These chips move data with light
scenes.narration: Silicon photonics uses light rather than only electrical signals to transmit and process information on a chip.

scenes.title: Traditional versions are rigid and opaque
scenes.narration: Conventional silicon photonic chips are powerful, but their rigid and opaque form makes them difficult to integrate into curved or body-worn devices.

scenes.title: The new process can scale beyond a few devices
scenes.narration: The researchers say their fabrication approach can produce many high-performance photonic components rather than only a handful of laboratory prototypes.

scenes.title: Think wearable sensors and transparent AR
scenes.narration: Future uses could include health monitors that conform to the body or transparent augmented-reality displays that follow the curve of a helmet.

scenes.title: A chip may no longer have to be a rigid rectangle
scenes.narration: If performance and form both become flexible, future chips could disappear into clothing, skin-mounted devices, or transparent surfaces.
